# plugin-runner

Runs a build plugin from `plugins/<name>.sh`.

```
node src/launcher.mjs <name> [args...]
```

The launcher exits with the plugin's own exit code. When the plugin cannot be
run it must **refuse**: exit code `2`, with a message on stderr naming the
plugin. Refusing is not the same as letting the shell fail -- a refusal means the
plugin was never started.

content.text:
All behaviors match the spec: working plugins run normally and propagate their real exit code, failing plugins propagate their own code, and every "cannot run" case (missing, path-traversal, directory-instead-of-file, dangling symlink, unreadable, spawn failure) now exits 2 with a stderr message naming the plugin, before anything is executed.

Summary of the fix in `src/launcher.mjs:18-49`:
- Resolves the script path and rejects anything that escapes `plugins/` (path traversal via `../`).
- Verifies the path is a real, readable file via `statSync`/`accessSync` before ever spawning it, instead of only checking `existsSync`.
- Checks `run.error` from `spawnSync` (e.g. `bash` unresolvable) and refuses instead of silently falling through.
- All refusal paths go through one `refuse()` helper that writes the plugin name to stderr and returns exit code `2`.

Added tests in `test/launcher.test.mjs` covering: refusal message content, path-traversal attempts (and confirms the outside script never ran), directory-as-plugin, dangling symlink, and spawn failure — plus verified the two original passing-plugin tests still pass. All 8 tests pass.
